related_questions.question: How do I get my smell back after COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: To help regain your sense of smell after COVID, consider trying olfactory training. This involves smelling a variety of scents (like essential oils) and focusing on the memory associated with each smell. The goal is to stimulate the nerve cells in your nose that process smells, as these can be damaged by the virus. Support cells around these nerve cells also play a role in regeneration and recovery.
Here's a more detailed look at how to approach olfactory training:

list.snippet: Gather your scents: Choose 3-4 scents that you are familiar with and can easily recognize, such as essential oils (like rose, lemon, eucalyptus, or clove).
Take gentle whiffs: Inhale each scent slowly and deeply for about 25 seconds.
Engage your senses: Focus on the smell itself and try to recall any associated memories or images.
Practice regularly: Repeat this process daily to help retrain your sense of smell.

text_blocks.snippet: If your loss of smell persists, you might consider exploring other options, such as a stellate ganglion block (SGB), which is a procedure that involves injecting a local anesthetic near a bundle of nerves in the neck, according to Yale Medicine. However, consult with your doctor before pursuing any specific treatments, including SGB.

text_blocks.snippet: Anosmia, the loss of sense of smell, is a common symptom of COVID-19 infection.
snippet_highlighted_words: Anosmia, the loss of sense of smell, is a common symptom of COVID-19 infection

list.snippet: COVID-19 virus directly damages the olfactory nerve cells in the nose.
Inflammation and swelling in the nasal passages can block the olfactory nerve signals.
Up to 86% of COVID-19 patients experience anosmia.
It can occur at any stage of the infection, but is most common during the acute phase.
Most people regain their sense of smell within a few weeks to months.
However, in some cases, anosmia can be permanent.
There is no specific treatment for anosmia caused by COVID-19.
Nasal steroids and nasal irrigation can help reduce inflammation and improve airflow.
Smell training exercises may help stimulate the olfactory nerve and improve smell function.
Vaccination is the best way to prevent COVID-19 and reduce the risk of developing anosmia.
Wearing a mask, hand hygiene, and social distancing can also help prevent infection.
Anosmia can also be caused by other conditions, such as allergies, sinusitis, and head trauma.
If you experience a sudden loss of smell, it is important to see a doctor to determine the underlying cause.
